findings.text: kanban/tickets/5.2.budget-stop.md: ticket 5.2 is done but the finding homed here from 5.1 is unaddressed in its Log: AC-4 test asserts only two substrings; tree, questions, plan page, Gate 1 unpinned. tests/test_grill_skill.py:126
findings.consequence: Whoever ships 5.2 carries an unanswered review finding into main. The next person reading 5.2's Log sees no record of it being judged or waived.

findings.text: brief_seconds returns 0.0 when brief missing or git fails, scripts/runner.py:655
findings.consequence: Someone reading traces/lanes.jsonl to compare lane speed cannot tell a real fast ship from a failed measurement: both read 0.0 seconds. Nothing in the file or on stdout says the brief was never found.

findings.text: human_touches is Log.waivers() count; one-waive fixture cannot show non-waive human entries counted, scripts/runner.py:674
findings.consequence: Anyone judging whether the light lane cut human involvement may read a touch count that omits human Log entries other than waives. The packet does not show Log.waivers(), so the number's meaning is unverified.

findings.text: Docs tests assert bare lowercase substrings over the whole file; charter/package match text elsewhere, tests/test_runner.py LightLaneDocsTest
findings.consequence: The docs guard can stay green after someone deletes the light-lane section from README.md, because the words it looks for occur elsewhere in the file. A newcomer would then find no description of the lane.

findings.text: Only the write is guarded; find_ticket, Log.parse, light_diff_lines run outside the try, scripts/runner.py:670
findings.consequence: A run that reached ship can still end in a crash if the ticket's Log does not parse, since measurement now happens on the ship path. The packet shows no test for that case.
